# C3.S2 — Recomputing Loop-Invariant Values

*Level 2 card. Category [C3 Inefficient Iteration Patterns](../categories/C3.md).*

Recomputes values inside the loop that remain constant across all iterations, paying the computation cost N times instead of once. This includes calling functions in the loop condition (e.g., while i < len(list) recalculating len() every iteration), evaluating static conditions inside the loop body, re-deriving values that depend only on variables unchanged within the loop, and using multiple sequential loops over the same data when a single pass would produce all needed results. Hoist invariant computations outside the loop to pay the cost once.

## Example from the taxonomy

Example: Calling len(list) in the loop condition each iteration instead of caching n = len(list) before the loop; computing config["threshold"] * scale_factor inside every iteration when both values are constant throughout the loop.

## How to tell

The description above says what this root cause *is*. This says how to decide whether a particular piece of code has it. Work through the steps in order; every one has to hold, and you should be able to point at the code that settles each.

1. the expression is pure
2. none of the names it reads are rebound inside the loop
3. it is genuinely re-evaluated per iteration (not a `for` loop's iterable, which is evaluated exactly once)

If a step cannot be answered from the code in front of you, that is an answer: read further out until it can be, or reject the candidate and say which step you could not settle.

## NOT a smell when

The pattern is present but is the right call. If any of these hold, reject the candidate and record which clause applied.

- the expression only looks invariant because the analyzer cannot see a mutation through an alias
- the call is impure and its repetition is the point (e.g. polling a clock)
- the loop body rebinds one of its inputs on a path the analyzer missed

## The repair

hoist the invariant expression to just above the loop

Before:

```python
for item in items:
    if item.size > config.limits.maximum:
        flag(item)
```

After:

```python
maximum = config.limits.maximum
for item in items:
    if item.size > maximum:
        flag(item)
```

**Patch shape: `statement_local`** — change a few adjacent statements and nothing else.

That bounds what the repair *changes*. It does not bound how much code you may read to decide, and it does not mean the waste has to live in one place. A patch that rewrites everything cannot be attributed to any one root cause, which is the only thing this constraint is protecting.

## Neighbours

These root causes match similar-looking code. Open them before you decide, and pick the one whose repair is the edit you would actually make. If two fit equally well, pick either and say so — the repair is what gets measured, and forcing a distinction the code does not make helps nobody.

They are also where to look when this card nearly fits and you cannot write a repair from it.

- **[C8.S3 Missing Local Lookup Caching](../root-causes/C8.S3.md)** — C3.S2 hoists a *computation*.  C8.S3 hoists a pure *name or attribute resolution* with no computation attached.  `len(xs)` is C3.S2; `self.config.limit` is C8.S3.
- **[C3.S3 Inefficient Per-Iteration Setup](../root-causes/C3.S3.md)** — C3.S2 hoists something whose value is reused unchanged.  C3.S3 hoists an *object construction* that is rebuilt each iteration.

## Verifying it

The effect grows with **input size**, so it is measurable given a large enough case. Make the largest case big enough that one call takes milliseconds, not microseconds.

Workload hint: at least ~100k iterations, more if the expression is cheap

## Decision

1. Every `How to tell` step holds, and I can name the code for each.
2. No `NOT a smell when` clause applies.
3. This is not one of the `Looks the same, is not` cases.
4. No neighbour describes it better.
5. I can write the repair for *this* code, at this patch shape.
6. This code runs often enough for the saving to exist at all.

All six, or reject — and record which one decided it.
